abstract_draft: High-frequency VO2 pulse switching creates localized, sub-nanosecond electro-thermal-phase fronts that standard two-dimensional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can underresolve even when the governing residuals are correct. Phase 0 places the nearest architectural precedent in NeuSA (arxiv:2509.04966v2), whose global spectral neural ordinary differential equation targets canonical wave evolution, while adaptive spectral PINNs (arxiv:2605.04502v1) diagnose gradient scaling only in a stiff ordinary differential equation; neither supplies a spatially local material-time map tied to the phase-rate law. We propose Kinetics-Clock PINN (KC-PINN): an exactly monotone analytic Gaussian-basis clock whose derivative is coupled to the endogenous VO2 phase-rate magnitude, with the electric, heat, and phase residuals evaluated through the complete first- and second-order space-time pullback so no governing equation is replaced. The predeclared falsification asks whether KC-PINN improves locked whole-case out-of-distribution switching-time, front-topology, energy-balance, coupled-residual, and field errors over parameter-matched spectral, causal, weighting, hard-constraint, and generic coordinate-transform alternatives. Its negative control fixes `tau=t` and disables the auxiliary clock residual while preserving the field head, physical-residual code, samples, budget, and dormant clock parameters; the mechanism fails if gains survive that intervention or do not exceed generic transforms. If supported, the result would isolate a kinetics-specific representation mechanism for resolving two-dimensional pulse-driven VO2 fronts, not a general speed or memory advantage.
motivation.problem_framing:
The structural problem is that an endogenous switching law can compress most phase change into a small, spatially moving portion of physical time. In a two-dimensional VO2 device, different locations therefore advance through the transition at different rates while voltage, temperature, and phase remain tightly coupled. A network expressed only in global physical time must represent a sharp front and smooth background with the same coordinate, exposing the high-frequency and residual-conditioning weaknesses highlighted by arxiv:2602.19265v1 and the adaptive-spectral diagnosis in arxiv:2605.04502v1.

The closest architectural precedent, NeuSA (arxiv:2509.04966v2), adds a global spectral state and causal evolution for canonical wave problems, but it does not construct a spatially local clock from the material kinetics. The energy-dissipation phase-field PINN in openalex:W4403555504 avoids propagation failure by solving a static steady-state problem, so it cannot represent pulse-created event time or moving topology. KC-PINN instead uses a finite analytic Gaussian basis with error-function primitives to construct the local clock without numerical time quadrature: the original electro-thermal-phase equations remain authoritative, and every first- and second-order derivative is pulled back through the learned map, including all spatial Hessian and cross terms created by a clock that varies across the device.
motivation.why_now: Three recent strands make this narrow gap actionable at once: arxiv:2605.04502v1 isolates gradient-scaling effects in adaptive spectral PINNs, arxiv:2602.19265v1 consolidates the high-frequency failure mechanism, and semanticscholar:a1448fd2600739b73894f3b8d467bf9a9e9630b2 exposes sub-nanosecond VO2 electro-thermo-phase topology as the relevant physical regime. A named FEniCSx model can now supply controlled synthetic trajectories, while automatic differentiation can evaluate the complete local-coordinate pullback rather than approximating or dropping its cross terms. The opportunity is therefore not merely to add spectral capacity, but to test whether an endogenous kinetics-aligned coordinate removes the specific representation bottleneck under a retrieval-bounded novelty claim.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[0].what_the: NeuSA (arxiv:2509.04966v2) represents canonical initial-value problems with a truncated global spectral state evolved by a neural ordinary differential equation and causal physics constraints.
It did not learn a spatially local monotone clock tied to the material phase-rate law or pull a coupled electro-thermal-phase device PDE through that clock.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[0].structur: Its representation assumes a global spectral evolution coordinate and therefore lacks the endogenous, spatially heterogeneous kinetics signal needed to define local material time.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[1].what_the: The adaptive-spectral study (arxiv:2605.04502v1) varies Fourier frequencies and initial-condition gates to diagnose gradient scaling in a stiff nonlinear ordinary differential equation.
It did not transform the independent time coordinate of a two-dimensional coupled device PDE or retain the chain-rule terms induced by a spatially varying map.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[1].structur: Its diagnostic setting has no spatially resolved phase-kinetic right-hand side from which an endogenous local clock could be constructed and tested.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[2].what_the: The energy-embedded phase-field PINN (openalex:W4403555504) predicts steady ferroelectric microstructures by enforcing energy dissipation in a static formulation.
It did not retain pulse-driven dynamic evolution, switching time, or moving phase-front topology in the learned solution.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[2].structur: It handles dynamic PINN propagation failure by replacing the trajectory problem with a steady variational target rather than by changing how physical time is represented.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[3].what_the: The operando VO2 study (semanticscholar:a1448fd2600739b73894f3b8d467bf9a9e9630b2) resolves electrically steered conduction topologies and sub-nanosecond electro-thermo-phase dynamics.
It did not provide a PINN coordinate mechanism that solves the governing device fields or isolates kinetics-specific representation value on synthetic numerical evidence.
motivation.why_prior_stopped[3].structur: Its contribution is physical measurement and mechanism discrimination, not a differentiable PDE solver or a training coordinate derived from the measured kinetics.
motivation.what_changes_when_gap_closes: Closing the gap would make pulse-created event time, moving front topology, and electro-thermal energy closure jointly representable by one two-dimensional PINN without replacing the underlying equations with a static surrogate. That capability would connect the dynamic target regime exposed by semanticscholar:a1448fd2600739b73894f3b8d467bf9a9e9630b2 to a solver that can be evaluated on whole held-out devices or protocols, while directly testing whether the global spectral remedy of arxiv:2509.04966v2 is insufficient when kinetics are spatially heterogeneous. It would also establish a reusable conditional statement: when the local phase-rate magnitude is informative and the pullback is complete, coordinate adaptation can be attributed to material kinetics rather than to generic extra capacity.
core_claim: An exactly monotone analytic Gaussian-basis local time coordinate, coupled to the endogenous phase-rate magnitude and used with a complete first- and second-order PDE pullback, can reduce the representation stiffness of two-dimensional VO2 switching fronts without changing the governing electro-thermal-phase model.

sub_claims.statement: A finite Gaussian-basis clock with analytic error-function primitives, `kref>0`, and `kfloor=sqrt(eps_dtype)*kref` has an exactly positive time derivative and preserves pointwise invertibility; if `r_tau` is driven small where `|K_xi|` is large, fast physical transitions are stretched in the network coordinate, without an approximation guarantee.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Closes the mismatch between one global physical-time coordinate and spatially heterogeneous switching progress.

sub_claims.statement: Applying the full space-time chain rule to voltage, temperature, and phase retains the original coupled residuals, including all spatial terms induced by the local clock.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Prevents the coordinate substitution from becoming an unacknowledged change to the device physics.

sub_claims.statement: An identity-map control that fixes `tau=t`, bypasses the analytic clock branch, and disables the direct `r_tau` residual can distinguish kinetics-specific value from parameter count, generic coordinate adaptation, or unchanged PINN training machinery.
sub_claims.supports_which_aspect: Makes the proposed mechanism falsifiable rather than attributing any gain to a broad adaptive-coordinate family.

key_equations.description: The clock is evaluated by analytic Gaussian primitives, never finite time quadrature. Fixed knots `c_j`, spacing `w`, a declared positive reference rate `kref>0`, `kfloor=sqrt(eps_dtype)*kref`, and a training-validation-only choice `M_tau in {8,16,32}` make `tau_psi(x,0)=0` and `partial_t tau_psi=kfloor+sum_j softplus(a_psi,j)b_j(t)>0` exactly for the implemented map.

method_flow.high_level_pipeline: KC-PINN first freezes a nondimensional two-dimensional VO2 electro-thermal-phase contract, including pulse interfaces, so the coordinate cannot silently alter the physics. A coefficient network `a_psi(x)` instantiates an analytic Gaussian-basis cumulative clock whose error-function primitives make `tau_psi(x,0)=0` and `partial_t tau_psi>0` exact, with `kfloor=sqrt(eps_dtype)*kref` and `M_tau` selected only from `{8,16,32}` on training-validation cases. A capacity-matched field head predicts voltage, temperature, and phase from `(x,tau_psi,p(t))`; automatic differentiation constructs the complete first- and second-order temporal pullback and full spatial Hessian before the unchanged physical equations and `r_tau=partial_t tau_psi-sqrt(K_xi^2+kfloor^2)` are evaluated. All choices are locked before whole-case OOD scoring, and the matched identity intervention fixes `tau=t` while disabling `r_tau` to test whether any downstream gain requires the kinetics clock.

method_flow.steps.title: Freeze the physical contract
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Nondimensionalize the existing two-dimensional electrical, heat, and phase equations and freeze their constitutive functions, pulse input, initial and boundary conditions, and residual scales; add no new governing equation.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: It makes the local clock a representation change rather than a physics substitution and fixes the quantities used to grade coupled residual and energy closure.
method_flow.steps.input: Device geometry, pulse protocol, constitutive laws, and initial and boundary conditions from the named FEniCSx model.
method_flow.steps.output: Frozen dimensionless physical operators and training-only residual scales used by all later steps.

method_flow.steps.title: Construct the analytic positive-basis clock
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Evaluate a coefficient network `a_psi(x)` with `M_tau` spatial coefficients and form `tau_psi(x,t)=kfloor*t+sum_j softplus(a_psi,j(x))*B_j(t)`, where fixed Gaussian bases `b_j(t)` have analytic error-function primitives `B_j(t)`; predeclare `kref>0`, set `kfloor=sqrt(eps_dtype)*kref`, use `M_tau=16` by default, and select only from `{8,16,32}` on training-validation cases with ties resolved toward the smaller value.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: The analytic construction gives `tau_psi(x,0)=0` and `partial_t tau_psi=kfloor+sum_j softplus(a_psi,j)b_j(t)>0` exactly without finite quadrature, while the acyclic coefficient network never reads a predicted field.
method_flow.steps.input: Normalized spatial coordinates, fixed Gaussian knots and spacing, the declared positive reference rate `kref`, and the training-validation-only `M_tau` choice.
method_flow.steps.output: The strictly monotone local clock `tau_psi` and its exact automatic-differentiation derivatives.

method_flow.steps.title: Predict the coupled fields in clock coordinates
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Feed `(x,tau_psi,p(t))` to a capacity-matched solution head `h_theta` that returns voltage, temperature, and phase, then compute electric field, current density, and Joule heating deterministically from those fields and the frozen constitutive laws.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: A single shared clock retains the electric-to-Joule-to-thermal-to-phase causal chain, while the known one-sided pulse value enters only the solution head and the clock graph remains acyclic.
method_flow.steps.input: Spatial coordinates, the analytic clock from S2, the one-sided pulse value, and the frozen constitutive contract from S1.
method_flow.steps.output: Clock-coordinate fields `V_hat`, `T_hat`, and `xi_hat` plus deterministic `E_hat`, `J_hat`, and `QJ_hat`.

method_flow.steps.title: Pull back every required derivative
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Use automatic differentiation to compute the complete first- and second-order physical-time derivatives and the full `2x2` physical-space Hessian for each scalar field, retaining all `tau-pulse`, mixed spatial-clock, clock-gradient outer-product, and clock-Hessian contractions before taking any trace or divergence.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: A space-dependent time coordinate preserves the declared PDE only when every induced chain-rule term is retained with the correct tensor shape; pulse jumps are handled as interfaces rather than differentiated through.
method_flow.steps.input: The fields from S3, analytic clock derivatives from S2, and one-sided pulse values on open pulse-smooth intervals.
method_flow.steps.output: Physical-coordinate temporal derivatives, spatial gradients, full Hessians, Laplacians, and divergence-ready quantities.

method_flow.steps.title: Evaluate the original physics and kinetics-clock residuals
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Insert the S4 derivatives into the unchanged electric, heat, and phase equations and add `r_tau=partial_t tau_psi-sqrt(K_xi^2+kfloor^2)` on open pulse-smooth intervals. At each pulse edge, use one-sided pulse values, enforce continuity of `T` and `xi`, solve the electric boundary-value condition on both sides so `V` may follow the imposed step, and retain the nonempty initial, boundary, constitutive, and interface residuals. Compute energy balance separately as a downstream diagnostic, not as an added training residual.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: This preserves the declared electro-thermal-phase model while making the clock kinetics-specific; when both the phase and clock residuals vanish, |∂ξ/∂τ|=|Kξ|/sqrt(Kξ²+kfloor²)<1 is a conditional property, not an approximation guarantee.
method_flow.steps.input: Pulled-back derivatives from S4, the frozen physical contract from S1, and the phase-kinetic right-hand side evaluated from S3 fields.
method_flow.steps.output: Scale-ready electric, heat, phase, clock, initial, boundary, constitutive, and interface residuals, plus a separately reported energy-balance diagnostic.

method_flow.steps.title: Match capacity, samples, and training budget
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Shrink the solution head to pay for the clock network so total parameter allocation is matched, then keep nonempty collocation sets, residual normalizations, update count, stopping rule, optimizer settings, wall-time cap, and checkpoint selection criterion fixed across arms; jointly optimize clock and field parameters from the first update.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: Reallocating rather than adding capacity prevents parameter count or a different training contract from masquerading as a clock effect.
method_flow.steps.input: The S1 residual scales, S2 clock, S3 field head, S5 residuals, and the predeclared common budget.
method_flow.steps.output: Capacity- and budget-matched KC-PINN checkpoints selected only by the in-distribution validation criterion.

method_flow.steps.title: Train mandatory same-bottleneck baselines
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Under the matched S6 contract, train a same-architecture analytic monotone coordinate transform that retains the complete pullback and the unchanged phase residual containing `K_xi` but omits the `K_xi`-driven clock coupling (`k_eff` and `r_tau`), an unmodified-coordinate MLP-PINN, analytic fixed transforms, fixed-Fourier and adaptive-spectral PINNs, causal PINN and NeuSA, self-adaptive and loss-conditional weighting, and hard-constraint/AdamFLIP comparators.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: The candidate survives only if the kinetics-specific clock adds value beyond generic learned coordinates, analytic time warps, spectral capacity, causality, loss weighting, and hard constraints.
method_flow.steps.input: The frozen physical and budget contracts plus the predeclared comparator definitions.
method_flow.steps.output: Matched baseline checkpoints for the same training-validation cases.

method_flow.steps.title: Run the matched identity intervention
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Instantiate the same clock tensors but freeze and bypass them with `tau=t`, disable `r_tau`, retain the identical solution-head architecture and nominal parameter and memory allocation, and keep samples, pullback code, update count, wall-time cap, optimizer settings, and physical residual implementation unchanged; report both nominal and active-trainable counts.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: This sole negative-control intervention tests whether downstream gains require the kinetics clock rather than dormant parameters or differently coded physics; a widened unmodified-coordinate arm in S7 separately provides active-parameter-matched performance.
method_flow.steps.input: The S2-S6 implementation with the clock-control switch set to identity.
method_flow.steps.output: A capacity- and code-matched `tau=t` intervention arm with `r_tau` disabled.

method_flow.steps.title: Validate in distribution and lock every choice
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Decode all arms at requested physical times and report field error, switching-time error, phase-front Hausdorff and topology error, energy-balance error, worst normalized coupled residual, wall time, and memory on training-validation cases; then freeze architecture, `M_tau`, hyperparameters, thresholds, metric definitions, and stopping rule.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: All estimands must remain physical-time functionals, and no formal-OOD result may influence model or evaluation choices.
method_flow.steps.input: KC-PINN, identity-control, and baseline checkpoints plus the in-distribution validation cases.
method_flow.steps.output: Physical-time validation metrics and a locked solver-and-scoring contract.

method_flow.steps.title: Score locked whole-case OOD
method_flow.steps.what_changes: Apply the locked solver procedure independently to each held-out whole geometry, material combination, and pulse protocol, then compare the same physical-time field, switching, front, energy, and coupled-residual metrics without changing the clock, field head, baselines, thresholds, or stopping rule.
method_flow.steps.why_this_step: Whole-entity post-lock scoring tests generalization without leakage and bounds any positive conclusion to synthetic numerical evidence for the declared VO2 model.
method_flow.steps.input: The S9 locked contract and untouched formal-OOD whole cases.
method_flow.steps.output: A bounded synthetic-numerical OOD result, not an experimental-validation claim.

method_flow.design_reasoning_echo: The design treats local phase-kinetic magnitude as an endogenous proxy for where physical time is representationally compressed; that premise is untested and is the falsification target, not an asserted material law. The forward graph remains acyclic because `a_psi(x)` produces the analytic Gaussian-basis clock without reading predicted fields, while the predicted kinetics enter afterward only through `r_tau=partial_t tau_psi-sqrt(K_xi^2+kfloor^2)`. The estimands are the physical voltage, temperature, and phase fields on complete device trajectories, with switching time, front topology, energy balance, and coupled residuals derived from those fields; synthetic collocation and reference trajectories come from the named FEniCSx model and remain split by whole case. A naive capacity increase or generic learned transform may already help, so the contribution survives only if the exact kinetics-coupled clock beats those alternatives and loses its downstream advantage when the identity intervention fixes `tau=t` and disables `r_tau`.
feasibility_validation.data.rationale: No closed data are required because the named FEniCSx model supplies the synthetic two-dimensional trajectories, while public VO2 measurements are contextual targets rather than training evidence.
feasibility_validation.theoretical.ratio: Pointwise temporal invertibility follows exactly from the analytic positive-basis clock, but the implementation must still verify every displayed second-order temporal and full spatial-Hessian pullback term and each one-sided pulse-interface condition.
feasibility_validation.engineering.ratio: The binding implementation cost is stable nested automatic differentiation through a spatially varying clock inside coupled divergence operators, although it fits the stated single-GPU bounded workflow.
feasibility_validation.falsification.rat: The locked whole-case scoring is concrete, and the mechanism intervention is implementable by fixing `tau=t`, disabling the auxiliary residual `r_tau`, retaining dormant clock tensors, and leaving the field head and physical-residual code unchanged.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[0].respo: The Phase 3.2 rationale already concedes that broad learned adaptive-coordinate novelty is occupied by R-adaptive DeepONet; accordingly, the `core_claim`, S2-S5, and E1-E5 bind the contribution to an analytic, spatially local clock coupled to endogenous VO2 kinetics and a complete pullback of the unchanged coupled PDE. The S8 identity control fixes `tau=t`, disables `r_tau`, retains dormant clock tensors for nominal-count parity, and leaves the field head plus all physical residuals unchanged; failure against this control or the generic learned and analytic transforms defeats the kinetics-specific claim.
reviewer_concerns_and_responses[1].respo: Novelty remains retrieval-bounded and unverified against intrinsic-time, material-time, and reaction-progress-variable methods. A targeted scoop-check must establish that no retrieved work already combines an endogenous phase-rate-driven spatially local monotone clock, full electro-thermal-phase PDE pullback, and the same identity intervention; an exact match would subsume the novelty claim, while a partial match would require narrowing it to the remaining interface delta.
domain_landscape.position_note: The candidate uses the area's mid-frequency architectural-operator-substitution pattern, but positions it as a kinetics-conditioned local time representation rather than joining the more common structural-prior or generic spectral-capacity variants.
